project.name: Drunkendub
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full strict-boundary audit. The local HES set contains four listed records: the 1842 wheelwright workshop lies inside Drunkendub and is visible; Newton House, its early-19th-century lodge and the 1704-dated Cairnton farmhouse lie only in the surrounding context and remain stored but map-hidden. All four now carry material dates without changing map names. No attraction reached the 60-point publication threshold. No qualifying cafe-led food stop, named local trail, managed picnic area, dedicated visitor parking or public toilet was verified. Treasure Trails lists only Dundee, Forfar and Montrose in its current Dundee and Angus collection, with no Drunkendub product. Angus-wide full audit completed 2026-09-01: all six visitor categories, the four named commercial trail providers, current official/conventional routes, strict-boundary scoring and local HES/NRHE integrity were checked.

townGuide.headline: A named locality rather than a developed visitor stop
townGuide.intro: Drunkendub remains at 20% after a complete settlement, practical and heritage audit. Its 1842 wheelwright workshop is valid local heritage, but a single private historic building does not make the locality independently worth visiting.
